mainEntity.name: Does it read JSON with comments or JSON5?

page_text:
Edit JSON online, as code and as a tree

The JSON Editor shows your JSON code and the data as a tree side by side. Fold objects and arrays, see the type and the number of entries of every value, and change keys and values right in the tree - the change goes into the code at exactly that place, and the rest of the file keeps its formatting. Errors are listed with line and column, and the data can be checked against a JSON Schema and converted to YAML, CSV or XML.

Everything runs in your browser. Your documents are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Code and tree

Highlighted JSON on the left, the foldable tree in the middle. A click in the tree jumps to the code, the code cursor marks its value in the tree, the path ($.items[3].name) is always shown.

Edit in the tree

Change keys and values, add, duplicate, move and remove entries, change a type - each as a small edit of the code, one step for Undo.

Errors you can find

A missing comma or quote, duplicate keys and values that do not fit your JSON Schema, each with its line and column. JSON with comments and JSON5 are read too.

Search

Search keys and values; every match is marked in the tree, Enter goes to the next one.

Convert

Format, minify and sort keys, or convert to YAML, CSV (an array of objects is a table) and XML. YAML, CSV and XML files open as JSON.

Many documents

Keep any number of documents in your browser, with their own undo history, and download them all as a ZIP.

How it works

  1. Start - choose a template under "New", open a .json file or paste JSON.
  2. Edit - in the code or in the tree; both always show the same data.
  3. Check and export - fix the listed problems, choose a schema, and download JSON, YAML, CSV or text.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

Embed the editor on your website →

Frequently asked questions

No. The editor runs in your browser and keeps your documents there, not on our server. A document goes to a server only if you set up a webhook to your own server, if a website that embeds the editor saves it on its own server, or if another website opens it here with a form (post.php) - our server then passes it straight to your browser without storing it. As on any website, the server logs each visit, and we count page views anonymously - see the privacy policy.

Does it read JSON with comments or JSON5?

Yes. Comments, trailing commas, single quotes and keys without quotes are read and shown in the tree, with a note that they are not plain JSON. "Format" writes plain JSON.

Yes, in the Convert tab or under Export. CSV needs an array of objects - each object is a row. YAML, CSV and XML files you open are converted to JSON.

embed.h1: Embed the JSON Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the JSON Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the document in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://json.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/config/app.json&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor: "json", event: "save", id, name, content, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in jsoneditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://json.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/config/$name.json", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says jsoneditor:ready, your page answers with jsoneditor:load, the editor reports jsoneditor:loaded, jsoneditor:change on real edits and jsoneditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send jsoneditor:get (the current state) or jsoneditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://json.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://json.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'jsoneditor:ready') {              // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'jsoneditor:load',
      name: 'Settings',
      content: await (await fetch('/config/app.json')).text()
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'jsoneditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';   // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'jsoneditor:save') {               // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as jsoneditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'jsoneditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://json.giit.ch/?embed=window", "jsoneditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. jsoneditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends jsoneditor:closing.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with jsoneditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'jsoneditor:load', name: 'Settings', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep every key. Only change values.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from jsoneditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'jsoneditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'jsoneditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'jsoneditor:load', name: 'Settings', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with jsoneditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://json.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.
